---
title: "One alpha, two lenses"
subtitle: "Catalog C-04"
description: "The same concentration parameter fixes how many clusters the J units occupy and how large the cluster of a random unit is. Only the first depends on J."
toc: false
---

A Dirichlet process mixture has one concentration parameter, alpha. In the Chinese
restaurant process it is a pseudo-count for tables nobody has opened yet: customer n + 1
opens a new table with probability alpha / (alpha + n) (see the
[restaurant](../dpm/crp.qmd)). The same alpha answers two different questions about the
prior.

- **Count view.** How many clusters do the J units occupy? K_J, the number of fitted
  components (occupied clusters), has a distribution that depends on alpha *and* on J.
- **Weight view.** How large is the cluster that a randomly chosen unit belongs to? Its
  population share W_SB is Beta(1, alpha) given alpha, whatever J is. Two random units
  share a cluster with probability rho = 1 / (1 + alpha).

## What to try

- **Start at Gamma(1, 1), J = 100.** The count view has mean 4.84 and variance 13.2,
  with a 90% interval of [1, 12]. The weight view gives Pr(W_SB > .5) = .591,
  Pr(W_SB > .9) = .303 and E(rho) = .596.
- **Move J from 10 to 500.** E K_J climbs from 2.65 to 6.44. The weight view and the
  gauge do not move: Pr(W_SB > t) = (b / (b − log(1 − t)))^a involves only a and b.
- **Try Gamma(1, 3).** More prior mass near alpha = 0 means fewer clusters
  (E K_100 = 2.50) *and* a bigger cluster for a random unit (Pr(W_SB > .5) = .812).
  The two views move together because they share alpha.
- **Switch to a fixed alpha** and drag it from 0.01 to 100. At alpha = 1, E K_100 = 5.19
  with variance 3.55: without a prior on alpha the count view is much narrower.

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
Elicitation of "about five clusters" targets the count view. Size-biased dominance,
Pr(W_SB > t), lives in the weight view. A hyperprior calibrated only on the count view
still decides the weight view, which is the unintended prior of
[Part 3](../problems/unintended-prior.qmd). These are prior statements.
:::
